why: Kahn's algorithm over names: a recipe's in-degree is the number of its ingredients not yet available. Start the queue with the supplies; each item that becomes available decrements the recipes that use it, and a recipe reaching 0 becomes a new available item.
hints: A recipe becomes makeable the moment its last missing ingredient appears. How can you notice that moment without rescanning every recipe?
Count missing ingredients per recipe and keep, for each item, the recipes that need it. That is in-degree plus adjacency: Kahn's algorithm.
Queue starts with all supplies; pop an item, decrement each recipe using it, enqueue a recipe when its count hits 0. Return the made recipes in input order. O(total ingredients).
pitfalls: Recipes on a cycle (or needing an ingredient nobody has) never reach 0 and are simply not made.
Return in the order recipes appear in the input, not in the order they were made.
